chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging is crucial for guiding personalized treatment strategies for laryngopharyngeal cancer. However, current clinical practice relies on invasive biopsy procedures, whereas CT-based staging remains challenging due to the complex patterns of tumor invasion. Recent computer-aided approaches face two key challenges: 1) Structural relationship modeling: existing methods underrepresent anatomically structured patterns of tumor invasion, as they either process whole CT volumes without tumor-specific anatomical constraints or rely on labor-intensive tumor segmentation. 2) Fine-grained cross-modal alignment: while radiology reports contain organ-specific invasion details, current methods that apply global feature fusion struggle to accurately align individual anatomical structures with their corresponding textual descriptions.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the specific research problem, including the clinical challenges of CT-based staging and the limitations of existing computer-aided methods (structural relationship modeling and fine-grained cross-modal alignment).

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: The framework comprises three key components: an Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG), an Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) module, and a Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) module.
chk_method.reason: The poster explicitly names and describes the three key components of the proposed anatomy-aware multimodal framework (AOG, OCA, and REG).

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: We collect the first and largest dataset for CT-based laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging, comprising 656 patients across four medical centers, all paired with CT reports for multimodal assessment (prior studies are single-center with 118-319 patients and imaging only). Cohorts: (1) Fudan University Zhongshan Hospital (FUZH), 439 patients with contrast-enhanced CT and reports (primary cohort, 5-fold cross-validation); (2) Chang Gung Memorial Hospital (CGMH), 25 cases; (3) Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University (EENT), 87 cases; (4) TCGA, 105 public cases. CGMH, EENT and TCGA form the external test set.
chk_data.reason: The poster details the multi-center dataset of 656 patients across four medical centers (FUZH, CGMH, EENT, and TCGA) with paired CT scans and radiology reports.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Implementation: PyTorch on NVIDIA H20; CT resampled to 1mm isotropic, resized to 128x128x128, HU window center 50 / width 450, intensities normalized to [0,1]; Adam optimizer, batch size 8, cosine LR decay from 1e-6 to 1e-7, weight decay 1e-5.
chk_setup.reason: The poster details the implementation setup, including PyTorch, NVIDIA H20, CT resampling to 1mm isotropic, resizing to 128x128x128, and HU window normalization.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Binary (Early T1-T2 vs. Late T3-T4): internal F1 80.83% / Acc 81.53%, surpassing the second-best MMI (77.59% F1, 78.57% Acc). External F1 76.46% / Acc 76.50%, outperforming TGCAM (74.09% F1, 74.38% Acc) by a significant margin.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster reports the binary classification results (F1 score of 80.83% and accuracy of 81.53% on the internal test set, and F1 score of 76.46% and accuracy of 76.50% on the external test set).

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Three-class (T1, T2, T3-T4): internal F1 61.43% / Acc 63.33%, improving over MMBCD (58.44% F1, 61.14% Acc). External F1 60.27% / Acc 63.78%, outperforming the second-best method by a large margin of 8.73% F1 and 7.78% accuracy.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster reports the three-class classification results (F1 score of 61.43% and accuracy of 63.33% on the internal test set, and F1 score of 60.27% and accuracy of 63.78% on the external test set).

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Comparison with image-only methods (SwinViT, VDPF, MRSN) and state-of-the-art multimodal methods (CPAM, TGCAM, MMBCD, LViT, MMI).
chk_baseline.reason: The poster lists the image-only and multimodal baselines used for comparison.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduced an anatomy-structured multimodal framework for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging that integrates CT volumes and paired radiology reports. By explicitly modeling anatomical topology through the Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG), performing organ-level cross-modal alignment via Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA), and incorporating structured clinical invasion knowledge using Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG), our method effectively captures organ-specific invasion patterns and their textual evidence. Extensive experiments on the largest curated laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging dataset and public benchmarks show consistent gains over state-of-the-art unimodal and multimodal baselines in both binary and multi-class staging, with notable gains over radiologist assessments. The framework also offers improved interpretability by aligning decision-making with clinically meaningful invasion pathways.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster provides a comprehensive conclusion summarizing the framework's performance, comparison to baselines/radiologists, and clinical interpretability.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Failure analysis (16/88 misclassified cases, Fold 1): over-staging (9/16, 56%) - in 7 cases the report explicitly described cartilage invasion not confirmed by pathology, reflecting CT’s known limitation in distinguishing tumor contact from true invasion; under-staging (7/16, 44%) - in 5 cases the report contained no invasion description or stated ’no evidence of invasion’ despite pathological confirmation.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster discusses the inherent limitations of CT-based invasion assessment (over-staging and under-staging relative to pathological ground truth) and mentions deployment considerations regarding segmentation models and institutional reporting differences.
